pull_requests.pr_title: feat: support agent setup via environment variables
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for configuring agent LLM settings via environment variables, which is particularly useful when using the CLI in CI environments where environment variables have already been exported.

## Changes

### New Environment Variables

- `LLM_API_KEY`: Override the API key
- `LLM_BASE_URL`: Override the base URL  
- `LLM_MODEL`: Override the model name

### Key Features

- **Environment variables take precedence** over agent settings stored on disk
- **Temporary override only** - environment variable specifications are NOT persisted to disk
- Overrides are applied to both the agent LLM and condenser LLM

### Implementation Details

- Added `get_env_llm_overrides()` function to read environment variables
- Added `apply_llm_overrides()` function to apply overrides to LLM instances
- Modified `AgentStore.load()` to apply environment variable overrides after loading from disk

## Testing

Added comprehensive tests in `tests/stores/test_env_llm_overrides.py`:
- Unit tests for `get_env_llm_overrides()` function
- Unit tests for `apply_llm_overrides()` function
- Integration tests for `AgentStore.load()` with environment variable overrides
- Tests verifying that overrides are not persisted to disk
- Tests verifying that condenser LLM also receives overrides

All 19 store tests pass, and 334 total tests pass.

## Usage Example

```bash
# Set environment variables
export LLM_API_KEY="your-api-key"
export LLM_MODEL="gpt-4-turbo"
export LLM_BASE_URL="https://api.openai.com/v1"

# Run the CLI - it will use the env vars instead of stored settings
openhands
```

Fixes #327

pull_requests.pr_title: (Hotfix): CLI crashes when opening MCP panel
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR fixes issue #362 where the CLI crashes when opening the MCP menu with the error:
```
TypeError: Object of type RemoteMCPServer is not JSON serializable
```

## Root Cause

The `_check_server_specs_are_equal` method in `MCPSidePanel` was trying to JSON serialize `RemoteMCPServer` and `StdioMCPServer` Pydantic model objects directly. When the agent's MCP configuration contains these objects (which happens when servers are loaded), the JSON serialization fails.

## Solution

Added a `_server_spec_to_dict` helper method that converts Pydantic model objects to dictionaries using `model_dump()` before JSON serialization. This ensures that both server objects and plain dictionaries can be compared correctly.

## Changes

- **openhands_cli/tui/panels/mcp_side_panel.py**: Added `_server_spec_to_dict` method and updated `_check_server_specs_are_equal` to use it
- **tests/tui/panels/test_mcp_side_panel.py**: Added comprehensive unit tests for the MCP side panel, including tests that reproduce the bug
- **tests/snapshots/test_app_snapshots.py**: Added screenshot tests for the MCP panel with various server configurations

## Testing

All tests pass:
- 11 new unit tests for the MCP side panel
- 4 new screenshot tests for the MCP panel
- All existing MCP tests continue to pass (100 tests total)

Fixes #362

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix cloud login to respect llm_base_url from settings
pull_requests.pr_body:
### Problem
`openhands login` fetches `/api/settings` from OpenHands Cloud, but ignores `llm_base_url` when creating the local Agent config.

This makes the CLI *always* display/save the default proxy URL (`https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev/`), even when the user configured a custom base URL (e.g. the `eval` proxy) in Cloud settings.

### Fix
- Resolve `base_url` from `settings['llm_base_url']` (fallback to the default proxy URL).
- Use the resolved base URL in:
  - the overwrite-consent prompt
  - the saved Agent LLM config (agent + condenser)
- Make `AgentStore.create_and_save_from_settings()` default to `settings['llm_base_url']` when `base_url` is not explicitly provided.

### Tests
- `python -m pytest`

---

pull_requests.pr_title: Add Critic Result Display in TUI
pull_requests.pr_body: ## Summary This PR adds support for displaying critic evaluation results in the OpenHands CLI TUI. It integrates with the experimental API-based critic system from [software-agent-sdk PR #1269](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/1269). ## Changes ### 1. SDK Dependency Update - Updated `pyproject.toml` to use commit `e9a84c57e3839192277293337c8c7312f41ace08` from the `xw/critic-model` branch - This commit includes the experimental API-based critic feature ### 2. TUI Enhancements #### Action Event Display - Added critic score indicator to action titles in collapsible widgets - Format: `[Action Title] [Critic: 0.85]` (color-coded: green for success, yellow otherwise) - Full critic evaluation details are displayed in the event content #### Message Event Display - Critic results are automatically included in message event displays - Uses the existing `event.visualize` property which includes critic formatting #### FinishAction Special Handling - When `FinishAction` has a critic result, displays the full event visualization - This ensures critic feedback is shown even for final agent responses ## Visual Examples When critic evaluation is enabled, users will see: **In Action Titles (collapsed view):** ``` [bold]Editing configuration file[/bold] [dim][Critic: 0.85][/dim] ✓ ``` **In Expanded Content:** ``` Critic Score: Overall: 0.8500 task_completion: 0.9200 code_quality: 0.8500 error_handling: 0.7800 ``` ## Technical Details ### Critic Score Display - Score is formatted to 2 decimal places in titles for compactness - Full details with 4 decimal places shown in expanded content - Color coding: - **Green**: Score ≥ 0.5 (success threshold) - **Yellow**: Score < 0.5 ### Integration Points - Modified `_build_action_title()` to append critic score when available - Updated `_create_event_widget()` to handle `FinishAction` with critic results - Leverages existing `event.visualize` property for full critic detail formatting ## Dependencies This PR depends on the critic feature being merged in the software-agent-sdk repository (PR #1269). Once that PR is merged, the `pyproject.toml` should be updated to use a released version or the main branch commit. ## Testing - ✅ Python syntax validation passed - ⚠️ Full integration testing requires a critic server endpoint - Manual testing recommended with a configured critic instance ## Notes - This feature is **experimental** and follows the status of the upstream critic implementation - The critic feature must be explicitly enabled by configuring a critic server URL and API key - No impact on existing functionality when critic is not configured ## Related - Software Agent SDK PR: https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/1269 - Implements critic result parsing and display as requested --- **Co-authored-by:** openhands @xingyaoww can click here to [continue refining the PR](https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/5da73f5640f34e00811ef2052467942a) --- ## 🚀 Try this PR ```bash uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@add-critic-display-in-tui ```

## What

Prevents emitting a dangling **Reasoning** header when providers stream `reasoning_content` tokens that are only whitespace.

## Why

Some providers send `reasoning_content` chunks like `" \n"` before any real reasoning (or before switching to normal `content`). The current logic treats that as truthy and emits the reasoning header with no visible content.

## Changes

- Only emit reasoning updates when `reasoning_content.strip()` is non-empty.
- Added a regression test covering whitespace-only reasoning chunks.

## Testing

linked_issues.title: Chore: create Devlopment.MD
linked_issues.body:
We should think about creating a development.md. This will serve two purposes

1. instructions on how to start developing on the CLI
2. expectations for code contributions, which will help set a review standard and let contributors know what will help get their PRs merged


Re point 2, possibly the following standards can be considered

1. Keep PRs minimally scoped; prefer to resolve one GitHub issue via multiple PRs when applicable
2. Include high quality test coverage (more discussion to be had regarding this)
3. Submit a screenshot/video demonstrating the new changes (create PR template for where assets can be dropped)
4. Err on the side of speed. De-risk large changes using feature flags

pull_requests.pr_title: Truncate long terminal commands in collapsed view
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

Improves the collapsed cell header display for action events with two enhancements:
1. **Truncates long terminal commands** to maintain single-line display
2. **Dims the detail text** (commands, paths) to create visual hierarchy

## Problem

When the agent executes long terminal commands (e.g., complex curl POSTs, multi-line heredoc file writes), the collapsed cell header would display the entire command, causing it to span multiple lines. This made the conversation history harder to scan.

Additionally, the summary text and detail text (like `$ command` or `Reading /path/to/file`) were both rendered in the same bright white, making it harder to quickly scan and distinguish the meaningful description from the implementation details.

## Solution

### 1. Command Truncation
Added truncation logic to `_build_action_title()` in `richlog_visualizer.py`:
- Commands longer than 70 characters are truncated with `...`
- The full command remains visible when the cell is expanded
- Multiline commands are flattened to a single line before truncation

### 2. Visual Hierarchy with Dim Styling
Added Rich `[dim]` markup to the detail portion of action titles:
- **Bold white**: Main summary text (e.g., "List all Python files in current directory")
- **Dim white**: Detail text after the colon (e.g., `: $ find . -name "*.py"`)
- **White**: Status checkmark (✓) remains bright

### 3. Unified Truncation Helper
Refactored existing truncation code into a reusable `_truncate_for_display()` method:
- Consolidates 8 separate inline truncation implementations
- Supports both start-truncation (for commands) and end-truncation (for paths to preserve filename)
- Uses consistent `MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 70` constant throughout

## Behavior Changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Long commands displayed in full, wrapping to multiple lines | Commands truncated to 70 chars with `...` |
| Summary and details both rendered in bright white | Details rendered in dim color for visual hierarchy |
| Inconsistent truncation limits (50, 57, 60, 67 chars) | Unified 70-char limit via `MAX_LINE_LENGTH` constant |

## Changes

- Modified `openhands_cli/tui/widgets/richlog_visualizer.py`:
  - Added `MAX_LINE_LENGTH` and `ELLIPSIS` constants
  - Added `_truncate_for_display()` helper method
  - Updated `_build_action_title()` to truncate commands and add dim styling
  - Refactored `_extract_meaningful_title()` to use the new helper
- Added comprehensive unit tests for truncation behavior

## Testing

All tests pass:
```
tests/tui/widgets/test_richlog_visualizer.py - 37 tests PASSED
```

Fixes #334

---

## 🚀 Try this PR

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@jps/trunc-long-cli-commands
```

linked_issues.title: Truncate long command-line invocations in collapsed view
linked_issues.body:
## Problem Statement

In the new visualization, most agent actions are displayed on a single line with details collapsed. This provides a clean, scannable view of conversation history. However, command-line invocations (terminal actions) are not truncated, which causes long commands to span multiple lines even when the cell is collapsed.

This commonly occurs with:
- Multi-line shell commands (e.g., file writes with `cat << EOF`)
- Complex curl POST requests with large JSON payloads
- Commands with many arguments or long paths

### Current Behavior
When a terminal action has a long command, the collapsed cell header shows the entire command, which can take up a dozen or more lines.

### Expected Behavior
Long commands should be truncated with `...` in the collapsed view so that each action takes up only a single line. The full command is visible when the user expands the cell.

## Proposed Solution

Modify the `_build_action_title` method in `openhands_cli/tui/widgets/richlog_visualizer.py` to:

1. Define a maximum display length for command text (e.g., 80 characters)
2. Truncate the command portion with `...` if it exceeds this length
3. Keep the full command available in the expanded content

### Implementation Details

The change is localized to the `_build_action_title` method, specifically lines 200-204 where terminal action titles are built. The truncation should be applied to the `cmd` variable before constructing the title string.

```python
# Before
cmd = self._escape_rich_markup(action.command.strip().replace('\n', ' '))

# After
MAX_CMD_DISPLAY_LENGTH = 80
cmd = self._escape_rich_markup(action.command.strip().replace('\n', ' '))
if len(cmd) > MAX_CMD_DISPLAY_LENGTH:
    cmd = cmd[:MAX_CMD_DISPLAY_LENGTH - 3] + '...'
```

This maintains consistency with other event types that show truncated titles (like `_extract_meaningful_title` which truncates at 70 characters).
linked_issues.author: jpshackelford

pull_requests.pr_title: feat(tui): conversation history side panel
pull_requests.pr_body:
### What changed
- Added an in-app Conversation History side panel toggled via /history and Ctrl+H.
- Implemented conversation switching from the panel with a persistent Loading toast that appears before loading and is dismissed after completion.
- Moved switch loading to a thread worker to keep the UI responsive.
- Improved History UX:
  - Title derived from the first user message (up to 100 chars).
  - Full conversation id shown as secondary info.
  - In-place highlighting for current and selected items (no list reload).
  - “New conversation” entry updates immediately after the first message while the panel is open.
- Added incremental loading in the history list: shows 10 most recent by default, “… More” loads 10 more.

### Cloud support
- If the user is logged in to OpenHands Cloud (token present), the panel also lists cloud conversations.
- Selecting a cloud conversation performs a best-effort resume by opening the cloud conversation URL in the browser.

### Test status
- make lint: ✅
- uv run pytest: ✅ (853 passed)

pull_requests.pr_title: Add external editor support with CTRL+X shortcut
pull_requests.pr_body:
Users can now press **CTRL+X** to open their preferred external editor for composing longer messages or complex input.

## How it works
- Press CTRL+X while in the input field
- Opens the editor defined by $VISUAL or $EDITOR environment variables
- Falls back to common editors (nano, vim, code) if env vars not set 
- Content is loaded into the editor, user edits and saves
- Content is automatically loaded back into the input field when editor closes
- Works in both single-line and multi-line input modes

## UI Updates
- Status line now shows "Ctrl+L for multi-line • Ctrl+X for custom editor"
- Clear indication of available shortcuts next to the input field
- Notification messages when editor opens/closes

## Implementation Details
- Uses CTRL+X to avoid conflicts with Textual's built-in key bindings
- Suspends the TUI while editor is open for clean experience
- Handles editor errors gracefully with user notifications
- Temporary files are properly cleaned up after use 

## Testing
- All tests pass (285/285)
- Comprehensive test coverage for status line updates
- Linting and type checking clean

This feature enables power users to leverage their preferred editor for complex input while maintaining the streamlined TUI experience.

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR implements the `/new` command which allows users to start a new conversation from within the CLI without having to close and reopen it.

Fixes #324

## Changes

### New Command: `/new`

The `/new` command:
- Clears all dynamically added widgets from the main display (conversation content)
- Generates a new conversation ID
- Resets the conversation runner
- Updates the splash screen with the new conversation ID
- Shows a notification confirming the new conversation started
- Scrolls to the top to show the splash screen

### Safety Check

If a conversation is currently running, the command shows a warning and does not proceed. Users must wait for the current conversation to complete or pause it first.

## Files Changed

- `openhands_cli/tui/core/commands.py`: Added `/new` command to the COMMANDS list and help text
- `openhands_cli/tui/textual_app.py`: Implemented `_handle_new_command()` method and added handler in `_handle_command()`
- `tests/tui/test_commands.py`: Added comprehensive tests for the `/new` command

## Testing

All existing tests pass, and new tests have been added to verify:
- `/new` command starts a new conversation with a new ID
- `/new` command is blocked when a conversation is running
- `/new` command clears dynamically added widgets but keeps splash widgets
- `/new` command updates the splash conversation widget with the new ID

pull_requests.pr_title: fix: Correctly format LLM model names for litellm providers
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes LLM provider routing issues when using providers like OpenRouter, Nvidia NIM, DeepInfra, etc. where model names already contain `/` (e.g., `openai/gpt-4.1` from OpenRouter).

Also cleans up the provider list by filtering out invalid "providers" that are actually vendor names.

## Problem

When selecting a provider like `openrouter` with model `google/gemini-3-flash-preview`, the model name was saved as `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` instead of the required `openrouter/google/gemini-3-flash-preview`. This caused litellm to fail with:

```
LLM Provider NOT provided. Pass in the LLM provider you are trying to call.
```

Additionally, the provider dropdown contained ~116 entries including invalid "providers" like `meta-llama`, `other`, `1024-x-1024` that were parsed from model names in the SDK.

## Changes

### 1. `openhands_cli/tui/modals/settings/utils.py`
- Always add provider prefix in `get_full_model_name()` regardless of `/` in model name
- This matches litellm documentation for all providers

### 2. `openhands_cli/tui/modals/settings/choices.py`
- Always include VERIFIED_MODELS providers (`openhands`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `mistral`)
- Filter UNVERIFIED providers to only include valid litellm providers
- Sort providers and models alphabetically, remove duplicates

### 3. `tests/tui/modals/settings/test_settings_utils.py`
- Added test cases for openrouter, nvidia_nim, and deepinfra providers

## Testing

All 603 tests pass.

## Before/After

**Provider list:** 116+ entries → 60 valid providers (sorted alphabetically)

| Provider | Model | Before | After |
|----------|-------|--------|-------|
| openrouter | `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` | `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` ❌ | `openrouter/google/gemini-3-flash-preview` ✅ |
| nvidia_nim | `meta/llama3-70b-instruct` | `meta/llama3-70b-instruct` ❌ | `nvidia_nim/meta/llama3-70b-instruct` ✅ |
| openhands | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | `openhands/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` ✅ | `openhands/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` ✅ |

HUMAN: this is a tiny detail that was found by OpenHands agent when it checked the code against the server code.

OpenHands server's `/oauth/device/authorize` response includes `verification_uri_complete` (a full verification URL already containing `user_code`). ### Changes
- In `DeviceFlowClient.start_device_flow`, prefer `verification_uri_complete` when present, otherwise fall back to `verification_uri`.
- When opening the browser, avoid double-appending `user_code` if it’s already present.

## Summary

This PR improves error handling in the conversation viewer by printing the raw JSON content when a validation error occurs while parsing event files.

## Problem

When viewing a conversation with events that have schema mismatches (e.g., extra fields not permitted), users only see a warning message like:

```
Warning: Could not parse event file event-00004-6f9b4ef0-c6e9-46e2-b385-93a9fbcd5a61.json: 1 validation error for Event
summary
  Extra inputs are not permitted
```

This makes it difficult to debug what's wrong with the event file.

## Solution

Now when a validation error occurs, the viewer prints both:
1. The warning message (as before)
2. The raw JSON content of the event file

This helps users understand what data caused the validation error.

## Changes

- `openhands_cli/conversations/viewer.py`: Modified `_load_event` method to print raw JSON when validation fails
- `tests/test_conversation_viewer.py`: Added test case to verify raw JSON is printed on validation errors

## Testing

pull_requests.pr_title: Add stale issues workflow
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary
This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow to automatically manage stale issues and PRs.

## Changes
- Added `.github/workflows/stale.yml` workflow that:
  - Runs daily at 01:30 UTC
  - Marks issues and PRs as stale after 40 days of inactivity
  - Closes stale issues/PRs after 10 additional days (50 days total) without activity

pull_requests.pr_title: Use LLM-generated action summary instead of string truncation heuristic + UI Clean up
pull_requests.pr_body: ## Summary This PR updates the CLI to use the new LLM-generated action summary feature from the SDK and improves the UI by combining action and observation events into a single collapsible block. **Show summary for tool calls** **Improved Markdown rendering** ## Changes ### SDK Dependency Update - Updated `openhands-sdk` and `openhands-tools` to use the `feature/action-summary` branch from [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk PR #1339](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/1339) (commit `19927a1`) ### UI Improvements #### 1. Combined Action-Observation Collapsibles - Actions and their corresponding observations are now merged into a single collapsible block - When an action is created, a collapsible is shown with the action details - When the observation arrives, the same collapsible is updated with the result #### 2. New Title Format - Terminal commands: `🔧 {summary}: $ {command}` - File operations: `🔧 {summary}: {path}` - Shows checkmark (✓) when action completes successfully - Shows error mark (✗) for errors/rejections #### 3. Content Updates - When action is pending: Shows action details (thought, command, etc.) - When action completes: Shows observation result only ### Example **Before (separate collapsibles):** ``` ▶ Echo hello world to terminal ▶ Terminal: [TextContent(cache_prompt=False, type='text'... ``` **After (combined with improved format):** ``` ▶ 🔧 Echo hello world to terminal: $ echo 'hello world' ✓ ``` When expanded, shows the execution result. ## Technical Details ### New Methods Added **Collapsible widget:** - `update_title(new_title)`: Update the collapsible's title - `update_content(new_content)`: Update the collapsible's content **ConversationVisualizer:** - `_handle_observation_event()`: Pairs observations with pending actions - `_build_action_title()`: Builds the new title format - `_build_observation_content()`: Extracts observation content - `_update_widget_in_ui()`: Thread-safe widget updates ### Action-Observation Pairing - Pending actions are stored in `_pending_actions` dict keyed by `tool_call_id` - When observation arrives, it looks up the matching action and updates the collapsible - If no matching action found, falls back to creating a new collapsible ## Testing - All 829 existing tests pass - Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff format, ruff lint, pycodestyle, pyright) ## Dependencies This PR depends on [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk PR #1339](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/1339) being merged first. Once that PR is merged, the SDK dependency should be updated to use the released version. Co-authored-by: openhands --- ## 🚀 Try this PR ```bash uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@feature/use-action-summary ```

pull_requests.pr_title: feat: Add toggle for default cell expand/collapse state
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

Closes #294, Closes #296

The CLI currently expands all sections (collapsible widgets) by default, showing full details of every tool call. The footer shows "^o Expand Cells" which is confusing since cells are already expanded. Users want:
1. A toggle to flip between expanded/collapsed modes
2. A setting to define their preferred default
3. Ability to expand/collapse individual cells (not just all at once)

## Solution

This PR implements:

1. **New CLI Setting**: Added `default_cells_expanded` boolean setting (default: `True`) to `CliSettings` model
2. **Settings UI**: Added a new "Default Cells Expanded" switch in the CLI Settings tab with clear description
3. **Click/Keyboard Toggle**: Click any cell title or press Enter to expand/collapse individual cells
4. **Arrow Key Navigation**: Up/Down arrows navigate between cells when a cell is focused
5. **Auto-focus Input**: Start typing at any time to automatically focus the input field (clicking cells doesn't disrupt typing workflow)
6. **Smart Tab Focus**: Tab from input focuses the most recent (last) cell instead of the first
7. **Clearer Keybinding**: Renamed the action from `expand_all` to `toggle_cells` and updated the footer label to "Toggle Cells"

## Technical Design

### Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `stores/cli_settings.py` | Added `default_cells_expanded: bool = True` field |
| `tui/modals/settings/components/cli_settings_tab.py` | Extracted `SettingsSwitch` component, added switch UI |
| `tui/widgets/collapsible.py` | Renamed from `non_clickable_collapsible.py`; added click-to-toggle, Navigate message, keyboard handlers |
| `tui/widgets/richlog_visualizer.py` | Added `_default_collapsed` property and `_make_collapsible` helper |
| `tui/textual_app.py` | Added `CollapsibleNavigationMixin`, auto-focus on typing, Tab handling |

### How It Works

1. When `default_cells_expanded = True` (default): New cells appear expanded (current behavior preserved)
2. When `default_cells_expanded = False`: New cells appear collapsed showing only the title
3. **Individual cell control**: Click any cell title or focus it and press Enter to toggle just that cell
4. **Keyboard navigation**: When a cell is focused, use Up/Down arrows to navigate between cells
5. **Auto-focus**: Start typing at any time and focus automatically returns to the input field
6. **Ctrl+O**: Still toggles all cells at once (collapse-all-or-expand-all behavior)
7. Setting persists across sessions via `~/.openhands/cli_config.json`

### Architecture

- **Renamed** `NonClickableCollapsible` → `Collapsible` (now clickable)
- **Message-based navigation**: `CollapsibleTitle` emits `Navigate` messages; `CollapsibleNavigationMixin` handles navigation logic in the App
- **DRY refactoring**: Extracted `SettingsSwitch` component and `_make_collapsible` helper to reduce duplication

### Backward Compatibility

- Default value is `True`, preserving current behavior for existing users
- Existing config files without this field will use the default (Pydantic handles this automatically)

## Testing

Added tests for:
- New `default_cells_expanded` setting in `CliSettings`
- Settings UI switch rendering and value retrieval
- `_default_collapsed` property in visualizer
- Collapsible click and Enter key toggle
- Arrow key navigation between cells and boundary conditions
- Test fixtures (`visualizer`, `mock_cli_settings`) to reduce boilerplate

---

## 🚀 Try this PR

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@jps/toggle-cell-collapse
```

---

*This description has been revised to reflect the evolution of the implementation, which expanded beyond the original scope to include individual cell toggle, keyboard navigation, and architectural improvements.*

pull_requests.pr_title: Skip PR description update for forked repos
pull_requests.pr_body: ## Summary This PR fixes the HTTP 403 error that occurs when the `update-pr-description` workflow runs on PRs from forked repositories. ## Problem When a PR is opened from a forked repository, the workflow fails with: ``` gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403) {"message":"Resource not accessible by integration","documentation_url":"https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#update-a-pull-request","status":"403"} ``` This happens because GitHub's `GITHUB_TOKEN` has limited (read-only) permissions for PRs from forked repositories as a security measure. ## Solution Added a condition to skip the PR description update job for forked PRs: ```yaml if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork ``` This approach matches how the main [OpenHands repository](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands) handles the same situation in their `ghcr-build.yml` workflow. ## Behavior After This Change - **PRs from the same repository**: Continue to have their descriptions updated automatically with uvx instructions - **PRs from forked repositories**: The job is gracefully skipped instead of failing @malhotra5 can click here to [continue refining the PR](https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/None) --- ## 🚀 Try this PR ```bash uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@fix/skip-pr-update-for-forks ```

pull_requests.pr_title: Exp: remote acp conversations
pull_requests.pr_body:
The ability to have a conversation with an openhands agent via ACP. The conversation should take place in a remote runtime in the cloud, and only supports V1 conversations. 

Clarifications required
- Do we want to support cloning the repository and checking out a branch; how would we identify the repo?


QA checklist that I've verified in Zed. You can use the following config to test this PR

```json
"openhands_remote_acp": {
      "type": "custom",
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": [
        "--python",
        "3.12",
        "git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@remote-acp-convo",
        "acp",
        "--cloud",
      ],
      "env": {},
},
```

- [X] Request to oauth if not logged in
- [X] Start fresh conversation
- [X] Resume existing conversation (started via ACP, or existing V1 conversation from cloud)
- [X] Confirmation mode
- [X] Sending a prompt to a conversation that has been open for a while resumes the sandbox 



#### Oauth if not authenticated
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f169ac81-32f9-4020-8499-69181da67710

#### Starting fresh convo + confirmation mode

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f01022d0-61cd-4d1e-9876-c52eb559f8d4




#### Resuming existing convo
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c018a1d3-4ca9-42a5-8d93-b48e15ca19a3


#### Resume a closed sandbox for conversations that have been open for a while 
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fc1e2e7-487a-46a0-ac4f-328e56e1d71b



Related to #269

---

This PR ensures that when the text wraps and the input box expands vertically from top when the text grows too long in single line mode

This video demonstrates the problem


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58390f16-94e3-4e38-b4b0-6e378f7f6ff6




This PR is a refactor of the input widget. It simplifies the code by using a custom `TextArea` for single line inputs, where the enter key submits content or interacts with an autocomplete dropdown instead of inserting a new line.  




### Changes QAed

Features confirmed that should still work
- [X] slash commands autocomplete and selection
- [X] files and directory autocomplete and selection
- [X] toggling between single line and multi line input and preserving text
- [X] Automatically toggle to multi line input when multi line text is pasted from clipboard

pull_requests.pr_title: fix: clipboard copy when copy button is pressed
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR implements the clipboard copy functionality when the copy button (📋) is clicked in the `NonClickableCollapsible` widget, following a similar approach to Toad's implementation.

## Changes

### Copy Button Functionality
- Added `on_button_pressed` handler in `NonClickableCollapsibleTitle` to post `CopyRequested` message when the copy button is clicked
- The `CopyRequested` message was previously defined but never posted - now it's triggered by button press

### Two-Layer Clipboard Approach
- **Primary**: `pyperclip` for direct OS clipboard access
- **Fallback**: Textual's `copy_to_clipboard` (OSC 52 escape sequence)
- This ensures clipboard works across different terminal environments

### Linux-Specific Error Handling
- Added `_is_linux()` helper function using `platform.system()`
- When clipboard copy fails on Linux, the error message includes a helpful hint: `"Failed to copy to clipboard. Try: sudo apt install xclip"`
- On macOS/Windows, the generic error message is shown without the xclip hint

Fixes #224

---


---

## 🚀 Try this PR

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@feat/clipboard-copy-button
```

pull_requests.pr_title: Add --resume and --last flags support to openhands acp command
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR fixes #260 where `openhands acp --resume --last` was failing because the ACP parser didn't recognize these arguments.

## Changes

- **acp_parser.py**: Added `--resume` and `--last` arguments to the ACP subcommand parser (same as the main parser)
- **simple_main.py**: Updated to handle resume logic for the ACP command, passing the resume conversation ID to `run_acp_server()`
- **agent.py**: 
  - Modified `run_acp_server()` to accept an optional `resume_conversation_id` parameter
  - Updated `OpenHandsACPAgent.__init__()` to store the resume conversation ID
  - Updated `new_session()` to use the resume conversation ID for the first session (if provided)

## Testing

Added tests to verify:
1. The ACP parser accepts `--resume` and `--last` flags (`test_acp_subcommand_supports_resume_flags`)
2. `new_session()` uses the resume conversation ID when provided (`test_new_session_with_resume_conversation_id`)
3. The resume conversation ID is only used once (`test_new_session_resume_id_only_used_once`)

All 655 tests pass.

## How it works

When `openhands acp --resume --last` is invoked:
1. The ACP parser now recognizes these flags
2. `simple_main.py` uses the existing `handle_resume_logic()` to resolve the conversation ID (e.g., getting the latest conversation ID when `--last` is used)
3. The conversation ID is passed to `run_acp_server()` which passes it to `OpenHandsACPAgent`
4. When the ACP client calls `new_session()`, the agent uses the provided conversation ID instead of generating a new UUID
5. The SDK's `Conversation` class automatically loads the existing conversation from disk

@xingyaoww can click here to [continue refining the PR](https://app.all-hands.dev/conversations/4fb7993d5e7c4daca2abe4c5fa36fa35)

---

linked_issues.title: openhands acp doesn't support --resume command when invoked via Toad
linked_issues.body:
## Description

When using Toad to launch OpenHands ACP with the `--resume` flag, the command fails with an error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `toad acp "openhands acp --resume --last"`

## Expected Behavior

The command should resume the last OpenHands session.

## Actual Behavior

The command fails with the following error:

```
Agent returned a failure code: 2 - usage: openhands [-h] [--version] [-t TASK] [-f FILE] [--resume [RESUME]]
                 [--last] [--exp] [--headless] [--always-approve |
                 --llm-approve] [--exit-without-confirmation]
                 {acp,serve,mcp,login,logout} ...
openhands: error: unrecognized arguments: --resume --last
```

## Analysis

It appears that `openhands acp` doesn't support the `--resume` and `--last` flags that are available in the main `openhands` command. These flags should be supported in the ACP subcommand to allow resuming sessions when launched via Toad.

pull_requests.pr_title: feat(mcp): Add enable/disable functionality for MCP servers
pull_requests.pr_body:
# feat(mcp): Add enable/disable functionality for MCP servers

## Summary

Adds the ability to enable and disable MCP servers without removing them from the configuration. This allows users to temporarily toggle servers on/off for testing or troubleshooting. This is especially helpful for cases where an mcp attempts to authenticate via oauth before every agent session--even when it is not needed.

## Changes

### Core Functionality
- **New utility functions** in `mcp_utils.py`:
  - `enable_server(name)` - Enable a disabled server
  - `disable_server(name)` - Disable an enabled server  
  - `is_server_enabled(name)` - Check server status
  - `list_enabled_servers()` - Get only enabled servers

- **New CLI commands**:
  - `openhands mcp enable <name>` - Enable a server
  - `openhands mcp disable <name>` - Disable a server

- **Enhanced add command**:
  - `openhands mcp add --disabled ...` - Add server in disabled state
  - `openhands mcp add --enabled ...` - Explicitly add server as enabled (default)

- **Updated list command**:
  - Now shows `[ENABLED]` or `[DISABLED]` status for each server

- **Store integration**:
  - `load_mcp_configuration()` now automatically filters disabled servers
  - Only enabled servers are loaded into the agent runtime

### Implementation Details
- Uses `enabled` boolean field in mcp.json (defaults to `true` for backward compatibility)
- Disabled servers remain in mcp.json but are filtered when loading configuration
- All operations validate server existence and provide clear error messages

## Testing

Added 12 comprehensive integration tests:

**Command Handler Tests** (5 tests):
- Enable/disable command handlers with success and error cases
- List command shows enabled/disabled status

**Parser Tests** (5 tests):
- Enable/disable subcommand parsing
- --enabled/--disabled flags on add command
- Error handling for missing arguments

**Integration Tests** (2 tests):
- Store filtering of disabled servers
- Behavior when all servers are disabled

**Test Results**: ✅ 88/89 passing (all new tests pass)

## Backward Compatibility

- Existing servers without `enabled` field default to enabled
- No breaking changes to existing commands or config format
- Existing mcp.json files work without modification

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Temporarily disable a server
openhands mcp disable my-server

# Re-enable it later
openhands mcp enable my-server

# Add a server in disabled state
openhands mcp add --disabled --transport http test-server https://api.example.com

# List servers (shows status)
openhands mcp list
```


---

---

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@jps/mcp-enable-disable
```

pull_requests.pr_title: Add workflow to update install-openhands-website on release
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds a GitHub workflow that automatically updates the version in the `install-openhands-website` repository when a new release is published in this repository.

## Changes

- **New workflow**: `.github/workflows/update-install-website.yml`
  - Triggers on `release.published` events
  - Also supports manual triggering with version input via `workflow_dispatch`
  - Updates the `VERSION` variable in `public/install.sh` in the `All-Hands-AI/install-openhands-website` repository
  - Creates a pull request with the version update
  - Includes duplicate PR detection to avoid conflicts

## Features

✅ **Automatic triggering**: Runs when a release is published (not draft)  
✅ **Manual triggering**: Can be run manually with a specific version number  
✅ **Version extraction**: Handles both `v1.6.0` and `1.6.0` tag formats  
✅ **Smart updates**: Only creates PR if changes are needed  
✅ **Duplicate prevention**: Checks for existing PRs before creating new ones  
✅ **Proper authentication**: Uses `INSTALL_WEBSITE_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret  
✅ **Comprehensive logging**: Detailed output for debugging and monitoring  

## Setup Required

Before this workflow can run successfully, you need to:

1. **Create a Personal Access Token (PAT)** with `repo` permissions that can access the `All-Hands-AI/install-openhands-website` repository
2. **Add the token as a repository secret** named `INSTALL_WEBSITE_GITHUB_TOKEN`

## How it works

### Automatic Mode (Release Published)
1. Workflow triggers when a release is published
2. Extracts version from release tag (removes `v` prefix if present)
3. Clones the install-openhands-website repository
4. Updates `VERSION="x.x.x"` in `public/install.sh`
5. Creates a branch and commits the change
6. Checks if a PR already exists for this version
7. Creates a new PR if needed

### Manual Mode (Workflow Dispatch)
1. Can be triggered manually from GitHub Actions UI
2. Requires version input (e.g., `1.6.0`)
3. Follows the same process as automatic mode

## Example Usage

After merging this PR and setting up the secret:

- **Automatic**: When you publish a release `v1.7.0`, it will automatically create a PR in install-openhands-website to update the version
- **Manual**: You can go to Actions → "Update Install Website Version" → "Run workflow" and enter a version like `1.6.1`

## Testing

The workflow has been validated for:
- ✅ YAML syntax correctness
- ✅ Proper secret usage
- ✅ Error handling and edge cases
- ✅ Both trigger modes (release and manual)

## Related

This addresses the requirement to automatically update the install script version when releases are made, ensuring users always get the latest version when running:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.openhands.dev/install.sh | sh
```

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR replaces the custom `load_project_skills` method in `AgentStore` with the upstream `load_project_skills` function from `openhands.sdk.context`.

**Depends on:** OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1420 (Add load_project_skills helper function)

## Changes

- Removed the custom `load_project_skills` method from `AgentStore` class
- Import and use `load_project_skills` from `openhands.sdk.context` instead
- Removed unused `Path` import

## Benefits

1. **Code simplification**: Removes ~25 lines of duplicate code
2. **Consistency**: Uses the same implementation as the SDK
3. **Maintainability**: Future improvements to skill loading will be centralized in the SDK

## Before

```python
from openhands.sdk.context import load_skills_from_dir

class AgentStore:
    def load_project_skills(self) -> list:
        """Load skills project-specific directories."""
        all_skills = []
        project_skills_dirs = [
            Path(WORK_DIR) / ".openhands" / "skills",
            Path(WORK_DIR) / ".openhands" / "microagents",
        ]
        for project_skills_dir in project_skills_dirs:
            if project_skills_dir.exists():
                try:
                    repo_skills, knowledge_skills = load_skills_from_dir(project_skills_dir)
                    project_skills = list(repo_skills.values()) + list(knowledge_skills.values())
                    all_skills.extend(project_skills)
                except Exception:
                    pass
        return all_skills
```

## After

```python
from openhands.sdk.context import load_project_skills

class AgentStore:
    # No custom method needed - use SDK function directly
    skills = load_project_skills(WORK_DIR)
```

## Requirements

Requires `openhands-sdk >= 1.6.0` (after OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#1420 is merged and released)

## Summary

This PR updates the CLI to use public SDK exports instead of importing from internal module paths, addressing issue #84.

## Changes Made

### Import Updates
- **ConversationExecutionStatus**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.conversation.state` to `openhands.sdk`
- **Event and MessageEvent**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.event` to `openhands.sdk`
- **Action**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.tool` to `openhands.sdk`
- **AgentContext**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.context` to `openhands.sdk`
- **LLMSummarizingCondenser**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.context.condenser` to `openhands.sdk`
- **Message and TextContent**: Changed from `openhands.sdk.llm` to `openhands.sdk`

### Files Modified
- `openhands_cli/agent_chat.py`
- `openhands_cli/runner.py`
- `openhands_cli/acp_impl/runner.py`
- `openhands_cli/acp_impl/agent.py`
- `openhands_cli/refactor/core/conversation_runner.py`
- `openhands_cli/setup.py`

- `tests/refactor/widgets/test_richlog_visualizer.py`

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test suite (`tests/test_public_api_imports.py`) to verify all public API imports work correctly
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Lint checks pass successfully

## Rationale

- **Stability**: Using the public API prevents breaking changes when internal modules are refactored
- **Maintainability**: Aligns with SDK CI checks that validate the `__all__`-exported API
- **Best Practices**: Follows the principle of depending only on stable, documented interfaces

## Notes

Some imports remain as submodule imports because they are not yet available in the public API:
- Security-related classes (`ConfirmationPolicyBase`, `LLMSecurityAnalyzer`)
- LLM constants (`UNVERIFIED_MODELS_EXCLUDING_BEDROCK`, `VERIFIED_MODELS`)

- Context utilities (`Skill`, `load_skills_from_dir`)

- Tool-specific classes (`MessageToolCall`)

These will be updated in future PRs as they become available in the public API.

## Testing

linked_issues.title: CLI crashes with XML parsing error when using Mistral models in confirmation mode
linked_issues.body:
## Summary
The OpenHands CLI crashes with an XML parsing error when using Mistral models due to improper handling of function call syntax in the action confirmation dialog.

## Problem
When using Mistral models, the CLI displays a confirmation dialog showing pending actions. However, the CLI attempts to display the raw function call syntax (e.g., `<function=execute_bash>`) in an HTML context, which causes an XML parsing error because the syntax is not valid XML/HTML.

## Root Cause
The CLI's `agent_action.py` has not been properly adapted to work with the new agent-sdk ActionEvent structure. Specifically:

1. The CLI tries to stringify `action.action` which can contain raw function call syntax
2. Even with `html.escape()`, the escaped content like `<function=execute_bash>` is still problematic for XML parsing
3. The CLI should use proper ActionEvent fields like `action.tool_call.name` and handle the display more robustly

## Impact
- CLI is completely unusable with Mistral models
- Users cannot interact with the agent when confirmation mode is enabled
- The error occurs before any actual work can be done

## Error Details
```
xml.parsers.expat.ExpatError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 1, column 75
```

The error occurs in `openhands_cli/user_actions/agent_action.py` line 40-42 when trying to create an HTML object with the action content.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. **Set up OpenHands CLI with Mistral model**:
   ```bash
   # Install OpenHands CLI
   # Configure with Mistral model (e.g., mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501)
   ```

2. **Start a conversation with confirmation mode enabled** (default behavior):
   ```bash
   openhands
   ```

3. **Send any request that would trigger a function call**:
   ```
   > what files do you see in pwd?
   ```

4. **Observe the crash**:
   - The agent generates a function call
   - CLI attempts to show confirmation dialog
   - XML parsing error occurs and CLI crashes

## Expected Behavior
- CLI should display the confirm
linked_issues.author: jpshackelford

pull_requests.pr_title: fix(cli): add terminal compatibility detection
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds a small, focused terminal compatibility check to the OpenHands CLI, without changing any existing public APIs or unrelated behavior.

The goal is to gracefully handle environments where the interactive TUI may not work correctly (e.g., non-TTY outputs, very limited terminals), while keeping defaults non-breaking and allowing automation to continue to work.

---

## Changes

- Added `openhands_cli.terminal_compat` with:
  - [TerminalCompatibilityResult](cci:2://file:///c:/Users/brass/OneDrive/Desktop/Work/OpenHands-CLI/openhands_cli/terminal_compat.py:5:0-9:16) dataclass (`compatible`, `reason`, `is_tty`).
  - [check_terminal_compatibility(stdout=None, env=None)](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/brass/OneDrive/Desktop/Work/OpenHands-CLI/openhands_cli/terminal_compat.py:19:0-52:5):
    - Uses [stdout.isatty()](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/brass/OneDrive/Desktop/Work/OpenHands-CLI/tests/test_terminal_compat.py:13:4-14:27) (if available) to detect TTY.
    - Treats non-TTY stdout as incompatible (TUI may not render correctly).
    - Treats `TERM` unset/empty or `"dumb"` as incompatible, even if TTY.
    - Returns a simple, structured result used by the CLI.
  - [strict_mode_enabled(env=None)](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/brass/OneDrive/Desktop/Work/OpenHands-CLI/openhands_cli/terminal_compat.py:55:0-58:67):
    - Reads `OPENHANDS_CLI_STRICT_TERMINAL` from the environment.
    - Enables strict mode for values like `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on` (case-insensitive).

- Integrated the compatibility check into [run_cli_entry](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/brass/OneDrive/Desktop/Work/OpenHands-CLI/openhands_cli/agent_chat.py:69:0-268:18) in `openhands_cli.agent_chat`:
  - Called **after** agent setup succeeds and **before** `display_welcome` and prompt session creation.
  - On incompatibility:
    - Builds a single explanatory message:
      - `OpenHands CLI terminal UI may not work correctly in this environment: {reason}`

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix MCP stdio server argument parsing with -- separator
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

The OpenHands CLI was unable to properly parse MCP stdio server commands that use the `--` separator to separate CLI options from command arguments. This caused "unrecognized arguments" errors for commands like:

```bash
uv run openhands mcp add local-server python \
    --transport stdio \
    --env "API_KEY=secret123" \
    --env "DATABASE_URL=postgresql://..." \
    -- -m my_mcp_server --config config.json
```

```bash
mcp add --transport stdio airtable --env AIRTABLE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY \
  -- npx -y airtable-mcp-server
```

## Root Cause

The issue was in the argument parsing logic where argparse doesn't handle the `--` separator well with subparsers when optional arguments (like `--env`) come after positional arguments (like `name` and `target`).

## Solution

### 1. Custom MainArgumentParser Class
- Created a `MainArgumentParser` class that extends `argparse.ArgumentParser`
- Added custom `parse_args()` and `parse_known_args()` methods that preprocess arguments before parsing

### 2. Argument Preprocessing Function
- Added `preprocess_mcp_args()` function that detects MCP commands and reorders arguments
- The function moves optional arguments (like `--transport`, `--env`) before positional arguments
- This ensures argparse can properly handle the `--` separator

### 3. Updated MCP Parser
- Changed the `args` parameter from `nargs="*"` to `nargs=argparse.REMAINDER`
- `argparse.REMAINDER` properly captures everything after the target argument, including handling the `--` separator correctly

### 4. Comprehensive Testing
- Added extensive unit tests covering various scenarios with `--` separator
- Tests cover both user examples and edge cases
- All tests pass and verify correct argument parsing

## Changes Made

- **Modified `openhands_cli/argparsers/main_parser.py`**: Added custom MainArgumentParser class with argument preprocessing
- **Modified `openhands_cli/argparsers/mcp_parser.py`**: Updated args parameter to use argparse.REMAINDER
- **Modified `tests/mcp/test_mcp_parser.py`**: Added comprehensive unit tests for stdio command argument parsing

## Testing

- ✅ All unit tests pass (13/13)
- ✅ Both user examples work correctly
- ✅ Arguments are properly parsed and stored
- ✅ Edge cases handled (e.g., `--help` arguments)
- ✅ Linting passes (format, lint, type checking)
- ✅ Backward compatibility maintained

## Verification

Both original failing examples now work correctly:

```bash
# Example 1
uv run openhands mcp add local-server python --transport stdio --env "API_KEY=secret123" --env "DATABASE_URL=postgresql://..." -- -m my_mcp_server --config config.json
# ✅ Successfully added MCP server 'local-server'

# Example 2  
uv run openhands mcp add --transport stdio airtable --env AIRTABLE_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -- npx -y airtable-mcp-server
# ✅ Successfully added MCP server 'airtable'
```

The fix ensures that stdio MCP servers can now be added with complex command arguments using the standard `--` separator convention, resolving the parsing issue completely while maintaining backward compatibility.

linked_issues.title: [CLI] The ability to list history conversation in CLI and show initial user prompt
linked_issues.body:
**What problem or use case are you trying to solve?**

After closing a CLI session, I would like to review the previous conversations I had, but there's no way to do this in the CLI.

AC: 
- When a conversation ends, we should show the conversation ID so it can be resumed

- Support a new command like`/conv` that will show the most recent 10 conversations from `~/.openhands/sessions` OR wherever the sessions are stored based on configurations.

It will basically list smth like:
```
- [CONVO ID 1] [Created at: XXX] Initial user message: ABCD...[truncated at 100 characters]
- [CONVO ID 2] [Created at: XXX] Initial user message: ABCD...[truncated at 100 characters]
```

- If the user has authenticated via their OpenHands Cloud account, we should also show the active conversations in the Cloud (active = a runtime is starting up or running) within the `/conv` list.
  - Related: https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands-Cloud/issues/205

Implementation notes: 
- You can find initial user messages by checking the JSONs ({0,1,2,3,4,5,6,...}.json in order) and look for `"action": "message"` and `"source": "user"` and get the `.args.content` field as the user message.

- We should allow the user to enter each conversation to view the [all user messages] from that conversation.

- We should also add a button and the button to move to next page/previous page.

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Overview

This PR implements OAuth 2.0 Device Flow authentication for the OpenHands CLI, enabling users to authenticate with OpenHands Cloud and receive API keys for accessing cloud features.

## Key Features

### 🔐 Authentication Commands
- **`openhands login`** - Authenticate with OpenHands Cloud using OAuth 2.0 Device Flow
- **`openhands logout`** - Remove stored credentials from local machine

## Authentication Flow

1. User runs `openhands login`
2. CLI initiates device flow with server
3. Server returns device code, user code, and verification URL
4. CLI displays instructions for user to visit URL
5. User authorizes via web browser
6. CLI polls server until authorization complete
7. Server returns API key
8. CLI stores API key locally


## Security Considerations
- API keys are never logged or exposed in error messages
- Device codes have short expiration times (10 minutes)
- Polling includes exponential backoff to prevent server overload

pull_requests.pr_title: Feat: `/condense` command to force compact conversation history
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR implements a new `/condense` command in the refactor UI that allows users to manually trigger conversation history condensation. The implementation includes proper async handling, error management, and event filtering.

## Changes Made

### 1. Updated Dependencies
- **Updated `pyproject.toml`** to use latest commit SHA `5ee81068fd16bb84d9a611e9af44825478155e15` from [software-agent-sdk PR #1368](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/pull/1368)
- **Regenerated `uv.lock`** with updated dependencies

### 2. Command Implementation
- **Added `/condense` command** to `COMMANDS` list in `commands.py`
- **Updated help text** to include the new command with description
- **Added command validation** - `/condense` is now recognized as a valid command

### 3. Async Condensation Logic
- **Implemented `condense_async()` method** in `ConversationRunner` class:
  - Runs condensation in separate thread using `asyncio.to_thread()` to avoid blocking UI
  - Includes proper error handling with user notifications
  - Prevents condensation when conversation is running
  - Provides user feedback for start, success, and error states

### 4. UI Integration
- **Added `_handle_condense_command()` method** in `textual_app.py`:
  - Validates conversation runner exists
  - Calls the async condensation method using `asyncio.create_task()`
  - Simplified error handling by delegating to conversation runner

### 5. Event Filtering
- **Filtered out `CondensationRequest` events** from visualizer:
  - Added `CondensationRequest` import to `richlog_visualizer.py`
  - Added filter condition to prevent "UNKNOWN Event: CondensationRequest" messages
  - Internal condensation events are now properly hidden from user

## Technical Details

### Async Implementation
The condensation process is now fully non-blocking:
```python
async def condense_async(self) -> None:
    # Run condensation in separate thread
    await asyncio.to_thread(self.conversation.condense)
```

### User Experience
- **Immediate feedback**: User gets notification that condensation will be completed shortly
- **Error handling**: Clear error messages if condensation fails
- **State validation**: Prevents condensation during active conversations

### Event Management
- `CondensationRequest` events are filtered out at the visualizer level
- `Condensation` events (results) are still displayed to show completion
- No more "UNKNOWN Event" messages for internal condensation events

## Testing

- ✅ All imports work correctly
- ✅ `/condense` command is recognized and validated
- ✅ Help text includes the new command
- ✅ Linting passes (`make lint`)
- ✅ Type checking passes
- ✅ Event filtering works as expected

## Usage

Users can now type `/condense` in the refactor UI to manually trigger conversation history condensation. The command:
1. Validates that a conversation exists
2. Checks that no conversation is currently running
3. Starts condensation asynchronously with user notification
4. Provides success/error feedback upon completion

This feature helps users manage conversation history length and improve performance when conversations become too long.

## Summary

This PR adds support for building macOS Intel binaries in addition to the existing macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) support, providing comprehensive coverage for all macOS users.

## Changes Made

### 1. **Updated Build Matrix**
- **Before**: Only supported `macos-15` (ARM64)
- **After**: Now supports both:
  - `macos-15` for ARM64 (Apple Silicon)

- **After**: 
  - `openhands-cli-macos-arm64` for Apple Silicon builds
  - `openhands-cli-macos-intel` for Intel builds

### 3. **Updated Release Assets**
- Modified the release preparation step to handle both macOS architectures
- Release assets will now include:
  - `openhands-linux` (Linux x64)
  - `openhands-macos-arm64` (macOS Apple Silicon)
  - `openhands-macos-intel` (macOS Intel)

## Benefits

- ✅ **Complete macOS Coverage**: Users with both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs can now use the appropriate binary

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix error display crash when error message contains XML special characters
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

When an error occurs that contains XML special characters (like `<`, `>`, `&`), the error display handler crashes with `xml.parsers.expat.ExpatError` because prompt_toolkit's `HTML()` formatter tries to parse the raw error message as XML.

This was seen when the agent state validation failed with a diff containing `'<missing>'` and `->` characters.

## Solution

Use `html.escape()` to properly escape XML special characters before passing the error message to the HTML formatter.

## Changes

- Added `html.escape()` call in the exception handler in `simple_main.py` (line 108)

## Testing

Added comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_error_display.py` with 4 tests covering:
- XML special characters (`<`, `>`, `->`, `{}`)
- Angle brackets
- Ampersands
- Quotes

### Test validates the fix

**Without the fix** (html.escape commented out):
```
FAILED - xml.parsers.expat.ExpatError: mismatched tag: line 7, column 81
```

**With the fix**:
```
4 passed, 2 warnings in 0.22s ✓
```

## Impact

- ✅ Error messages with special characters are now displayed correctly
- ✅ No more secondary crashes when displaying error messages
- ✅ Users can see the actual error instead of ExpatError

---

---

## 🚀 Try this PR

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@jps/fix-error-display-crash
```

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR refactors the E2E tests in `build.py` to separate them into individual files with structured result tracking using Pydantic models.

## Changes Made

### 🏗️ **Structure**
- **Extracted all E2E tests** from `build.py` into individual files in the new `e2e_tests/` directory
- **Created Pydantic models** (`TestResult`, `TestSummary`) for structured test results
- **Implemented centralized test runner** with detailed summary reporting

### 📊 **Test Result Tracking**
Each test now returns a `TestResult` object with:
- `test_name`: Name of the test
- `success`: Whether the test passed
- `cost`: Cost of running the test (currently always 0.0 as requested)
- `boot_time_seconds`: Time to boot the application (if applicable)
- `total_time_seconds`: Total test execution time
- `error_message`: Error message if the test failed
- `output_preview`: Preview of output for debugging
- `metadata`: Additional test-specific metadata

### 🧪 **Tests Extracted**
1. **`test_version.py`** - Tests the `--version` flag functionality
2. **`test_executable.py`** - Tests main CLI with welcome prompt and `/help` command
3. **`test_experimental_ui.py`** - Tests experimental textual UI with `--exp` flag
4. **`test_acp.py`** - Tests ACP server with JSON-RPC messages

### 🔄 **Backward Compatibility**
- `build.py` maintains the same interface and exit codes
- All existing functionality preserved
- Enhanced error reporting and debugging information

## Benefits

✅ **Better Organization** - Each test is now in its own file, making them easier to maintain and extend

✅ **Structured Results** - Comprehensive tracking of test metrics including cost, timing, and metadata

✅ **Enhanced Debugging** - Detailed error messages and output previews for failed tests

✅ **Extensibility** - Easy to add new tests by creating new files and adding them to the runner

✅ **Type Safety** - Pydantic models ensure consistent result structure

## Testing

- All imports work correctly
- Code passes linting and formatting checks
- Test runner executes all tests and provides detailed summaries
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing build process

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds a formatted `status_line` string to the metrics metadata that is sent with ACP session updates, along with the existing raw metrics. The status line provides a human-readable summary of token usage and costs, giving clients more flexibility in how to display metrics.

## Changes

### Implementation (`openhands_cli/acp_impl/event.py`)
- Added `_format_status_line()` method that formats metrics into a readable string
- Updated `_get_metadata()` to include `status_line` in the returned metrics dictionary
- The formatting logic is based on the SDK's default visualizer title implementation from `software-agent-sdk`

### Testing (`tests/acp/test_event_subscriber.py`)
- Added `test_get_metadata_with_status_line()` to verify status_line is included with raw metrics
- Added `test_format_status_line_abbreviations()` to verify large number abbreviations work correctly

## Status Line Format

The status line includes:
- **Input tokens** with abbreviation (K/M/B for thousands/millions/billions)
- **Cache hit rate** as a percentage
- **Reasoning tokens** (when > 0)
- **Output tokens** with abbreviation
- **Cost** with 4 decimal places

**Example:** `↑ input 1.2K • cache hit 50.00% • ↓ output 500 • $ 0.0050`

![Uploading image.png…]()


## Motivation

As requested, this gives clients the freedom to display metrics in a consistent, human-readable format without needing to know implementation details like currency formatting or token abbreviation logic. The client can either use the pre-formatted `status_line` or construct their own display from the raw metrics.

## Testing

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix multi-line paste issue in single-line input mode
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

When users paste multi-line content into the input field while it's in single-line mode, the content gets truncated or mangled because the single-line Input widget cannot properly handle newlines. This creates a poor user experience when pasting code snippets, error messages, or other multi-line text.

## Solution

This PR implements automatic mode switching when multi-line content is pasted into the input field while in single-line mode:

### Key Changes

1. **PasteAwareInput Custom Widget**: Created a custom Input widget that intercepts paste events and detects multi-line content
2. **Automatic Mode Switching**: When multi-line content is detected, the input field automatically switches to multi-line mode and sets the pasted content
3. **Comprehensive Line Ending Support**: Handles all common line ending types:
   - Unix/Linux: `\n`
   - Classic Mac: `\r` 
   - Windows: `\r\n`
   - Mixed line endings
4. **Smart Detection**: Only switches mode for actual multi-line content, preserving single-line behavior for regular text
5. **Integration with Existing UI**: Works seamlessly with the existing toggle functionality and UI layout

### Implementation Details

- Uses Textual's `@on(Paste)` decorator to intercept paste events at the widget level
- Emits custom `PasteDetected` message to communicate with parent InputField
- Only processes paste events when in single-line mode (ignores when already in multi-line mode)
- Preserves all existing functionality for manual mode switching and regular input

### Testing

Added comprehensive test coverage including:
- Unit tests for paste detection logic
- Integration tests using Textual's pilot app framework
- Tests for all line ending types
- Edge cases (empty paste, single-line paste, etc.)
- Verification that existing functionality remains intact

## Testing

All existing tests pass, and new tests verify the paste functionality works correctly:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/refactor/widgets/test_input_field.py -v
# 40 tests pass, including 6 new integration tests
```

## Impact

- ✅ Fixes the multi-line paste issue reported by users
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing API
- ✅ Comprehensive test coverage
- ✅ Follows existing code patterns and conventions

This enhancement significantly improves the user experience when working with multi-line content in the OpenHands CLI.

pull_requests.pr_title: Implement slash commands and confirmation mode for ACP

Slash Commands System (`slash_commands.py`) - ✅ `parse_slash_command()` - Parser for slash commands (e.g., `/help`, `/confirm always-ask`) - ✅ `/help` command - Shows all available commands - ✅ `/confirm` command - Controls confirmation mode with 3 modes: - `always-ask` - Request permission before every action - `always-approve` - Automatically approve all actions - `llm-approve` - Use LLM security analyzer to auto-approve safe actions - ✅ Commands sent to ACP clients via `availableCommands` in `SessionUpdateRequest` - ✅ Utility functions for mode validation, help text generation, and conversation configuration ### 2. linked_issues.title: Implement Slash Commands and Confirmation Mode for ACP
linked_issues.body:
## Overview

Following the [Initial ACP Implementation](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI/pull/69), we need to implement additional ACP features to enhance user interaction and control:

1. **Confirmation Mode** - Allow users to approve or reject tool calls and prompt turns before execution
2. **Slash Commands** - Provide a way for users to change confirmation mode and other settings during a session

## Background

The Initial ACP Implementation (PR #69) successfully implemented the core ACP features:
- ✅ Initialization
- ✅ Session Setup
- ✅ Content (including embedded content)
- ✅ Basic Prompt turns (except permission)
- ✅ Basic Tool Calls
- ✅ Agent Plan

However, two important features were deferred to future work:
- ❌ Confirmation for tool calls and prompt turns
- ❌ Slash commands for changing confirmation mode

## Requirements

### 1. Confirmation Mode

Implement user confirmation for tool calls and prompt turns as specified in the ACP protocol:

- **Tool Call Confirmation**: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/tool-calls
- **Prompt Turn Permission**: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/prompt-turn

**Expected Behavior:**
- Allow users to enable/disable confirmation mode
- When enabled, pause execution before each tool call or prompt turn
- Present the action details to the user
- Allow user to approve, reject, or modify the action
- Handle rejected actions gracefully

### 2. Slash Commands

Implement slash commands as specified in the ACP protocol:

- **Slash Commands Specification**: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/slash-commands

**Expected Behavior:**
- Support `/` prefix for commands
- Implement commands for controlling confirmation mode (e.g., `/confirm on`, `/confirm off`, `/confirm toggle`)
- Display available slash commands via `/help` or similar
- Handle invalid slash commands gracefully with helpful error messages
- Allow extensibility for future slash commands

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix URL display by adding newlines to prevent truncation
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Description

Fixes URL truncation issue where URLs displayed in the CLI were cut off in narrow terminals, as reported in the #p-toad Slack channel.

## Problem

When the OpenHands CLI prompts users for API keys or displays information about OpenHands models, URLs are displayed inline with other text. In narrow terminals or when terminals don't resize properly, these URLs get truncated, making them difficult or impossible to see and copy.

This was particularly problematic during the initial setup flow when users need to retrieve their API key from `https://app.all-hands.dev/settings/api-keys`.

## Solution

Added newlines (`\n`) before URLs to ensure they display on their own lines, making them fully visible regardless of terminal width.

## Changes

1. **Line 75-76**: Added newline before OpenHands LLM pricing details URL
   - Changed from: `"...no markup. Details: https://docs.all-hands.dev/usage/llms/openhands-llms"`
   - Changed to: `"...no markup.\n" + "Details: https://docs.all-hands.dev/usage/llms/openhands-llms"`

2. **Line 112**: Added newline before OpenHands API key settings URL  
   - Changed from: `"OpenHands Cloud: https://app.all-hands.dev/settings/api-keys\n"`
   - Changed to: `"OpenHands Cloud:\nhttps://app.all-hands.dev/settings/api-keys\n"`

## Testing

- ✅ All linters pass:
  - `ruff format` - No formatting changes needed
  - `ruff check --fix` - All checks passed
  - `pycodestyle` - No issues
  - `pyright` - 0 errors, 0 warnings
- ✅ All tests pass: `pytest tests/settings/` - 32 tests passed

## Visual Impact

### Before
```
You can find your OpenHands LLM API Key in the API Keys tab of OpenHands Cloud: https://app.all-hands.dev/settings/api-keys
```
(URL might be truncated depending on terminal width)

### After
```
You can find your OpenHands LLM API Key in the API Keys tab of OpenHands Cloud:
https://app.all-hands.dev/settings/api-keys
```
(URL always visible on its own line)

## Related

Addresses issue reported by @willmcgugan in Slack #p-toad channel regarding truncated URLs during CLI setup that required manual terminal resizing to view.

pull_requests.pr_title: Fix MarkupError with Chinese characters and special symbols
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

The CLI was experiencing a `MarkupError` when rendering content containing Chinese characters combined with special markup characters like `[`, `]`, `+`, and `%`.

Example error:
```
MarkupError: Expected markup value (found '+0.3%,月变化+0.8%,处于历史40%分位]\n').
```

## Root Cause

When `event.visualize` (a Rich renderable object) is converted to a string and passed to `Static` widgets with `markup=True` (the default), the Static widget attempts to parse it as Rich markup. However, when the content contains literal square brackets `[` and `]` (not meant as markup tags), combined with Chinese characters and other special symbols, the markup parser fails.

## Solution

This PR adds proper escaping of Rich markup characters before content is passed to Static widgets:

1. **New helper method**: `_safe_content_string()` that escapes square brackets in content strings to prevent them from being interpreted as markup tags
2. **Applied consistently**: All instances where `str(content)` was used have been replaced with `self._safe_content_string(content)` in the visualizer
3. **Preserves formatting**: Intentional Rich markup (like colored metrics with `[cyan]`, `[magenta]`, etc.) continues to work because it's added after the content is escaped

## Changes

- Modified `openhands_cli/refactor/widgets/richlog_visualizer.py`:
  - Added `_safe_content_string()` method to escape markup characters
  - Updated all event handlers (ActionEvent, ObservationEvent, MessageEvent, AgentErrorEvent, PauseEvent, Condensation, etc.) to use the safe string conversion

## Testing

- [x] Linting passes (`make lint`)
- The fix ensures content with Chinese characters and special symbols can be displayed without markup errors
- Intentional Rich markup in metrics displays continues to function correctly

## Related Issue

Fixes the Chinese character MarkupError reported in PR #141

pull_requests.pr_title: fix: hardcode base_url for OpenHands provider in CLI
pull_requests.pr_body:
## Problem

This PR addresses a breaking change introduced by agent-sdk PR #1273 (https://github.com/OpenHands/agent-sdk/pull/1273), which made the `base_url` configurable for the OpenHands provider.

Previously, the agent-sdk hardcoded the `base_url` to `https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev/` when the model started with `openhands/`. After the change, the SDK now respects any `base_url` passed in, defaulting to the proxy URL only if no value is provided.

The OpenHands-CLI wasn't passing a `base_url` when creating LLM configurations, which could cause connection issues when users select the OpenHands provider.

## Solution

This PR updates the CLI to explicitly set `base_url` to `https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev/` when users select the OpenHands provider (models starting with `openhands/`).

### Changes

1. **Updated `_save_llm_settings` method** in `openhands_cli/tui/settings/settings_screen.py`:
   - Automatically sets `base_url` to `https://llm-proxy.app.all-hands.dev/` for OpenHands provider models
   - Only applies the hardcoded value when `base_url` is not explicitly provided
   - Respects any explicitly provided `base_url` value (for advanced use cases)

2. **Added comprehensive tests** in `tests/settings/test_settings_workflow.py`:
   - Test that OpenHands provider models automatically get the correct base_url
   - Test that explicit base_url values are respected even for OpenHands models
   - Test that non-OpenHands providers don't get automatic base_url assignment

## Testing

All tests pass, including the three new test cases:
- `test_openhands_provider_hardcodes_base_url`: Verifies automatic base_url assignment
- `test_openhands_provider_respects_explicit_base_url`: Ensures explicit values are preserved
- `test_non_openhands_provider_no_base_url`: Confirms no side effects for other providers

## Related

- Related to agent-sdk PR #1273: https://github.com/OpenHands/agent-sdk/pull/1273
- Requested by @xingyaoww in https://github.com/OpenHands/agent-sdk/pull/1273#issuecomment

---

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 git+https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI.git@fix/hardcode-base-url-for-openhands-provider
```

pull_requests.pr_body:
## Summary

This PR improves the bottom status line layout by splitting it into two separate widgets and adding a friendly waving hand animation. It also adds `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+D` as alternative quit keybindings for better compatibility with VS Code.

## Changes

### 1. Split Status Line into Two Widgets

**Before:** Single status line showing all information on one or two cramped lines

**After:** Two separate widgets for better organization and readability:

#### 🔄 WorkingStatusLine (Above Input)
- Shows working status with animated waving hand emoji: 👋 🖐️ ✋
- Displays elapsed time and keyboard shortcuts
- Only visible when conversation is running
- Example: `👋 Working (5s • ESC: pause • Ctrl+O: expand)`

#### 📍 InfoStatusLine (Below Input)
- Shows input mode and work directory
- Always visible for quick reference
- Example: `Single-line • Ctrl+I for multi-line • ~/Projects/OpenHands-CLI`

### 3. Additional Quit Keybindings

Added `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+D` as alternatives to `Ctrl+Q`:
- **Issue:** `Ctrl+Q` doesn't work in VS Code (conflicts with editor shortcuts)
- **Solution:** All three shortcuts now trigger the same exit confirmation flow
- Improves user experience across different terminal environments

### 4. Visual Layout

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│        Main Display Area                │
│     (conversation history)              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
  👋 Working (5s • ESC: pause • Ctrl+O: expand)  ← WorkingStatusLine
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Message, @file, or /command             │  ← Input Field
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
  Single-line • Ctrl+I for multi-line • ~/Projects/...  ← InfoStatusLine
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Footer (keyboard shortcuts)             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Benefits

✅ **Better organization** - Working status and static info cleanly separated  
✅ **Improved readability** - Less cramped, easier to scan at a glance  
✅ **Brand alignment** - Waving hand animation matches OpenHands identity  
✅ **Better UX** - Multiple quit shortcuts work across different environments  
✅ **Clearer hierarchy** - Important working status prominently positioned above input  

## Files Changed

- `openhands_cli/refactor/widgets/status_line.py` - Split into WorkingStatusLine and InfoStatusLine classes
- `openhands_cli/refactor/textual_app.py` - Updated to use both widgets and added quit keybindings
- `openhands_cli/refactor/textual_app.tcss` - Adjusted input_area height for new layout
- `exit_modal_fix_summary.md` - Removed documentation file (not needed in version control)

## Testing

✅ All linting passes (ruff, pycodestyle, pyright)  
✅ Import verification successful  
✅ Code follows project style guidelines  
✅ Ready for manual testing in terminal  

## Screenshots

See commit for visual reference of the improved layout with waving hand animation.

---
